skill.name: module-scaffolder
skill.description: Scaffold DevPrep AI feature modules with TypeScript templates, folder conventions, component helpers, and validation scripts.
skill.summary: Creates and checks DevPrep AI frontend modules that follow project architecture and TypeScript quality rules.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are documentation examples, TypeScript imports, or Markdown code fences and are false positives. The real issue is unvalidated module names in add and validate scripts, which can permit path traversal outside frontend/src/modules. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: add-component.sh and validate-module.sh accept module names without the validation used by create-module.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Apply the same lowercase module-name regex, canonicalize paths, and reject any resolved path outside MODULES_DIR before reading or writing.

remediation.issue: The Bash helpers write project files directly when invoked.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode and print every target path before writes so users can review changes before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Module Name Allows Path Traversal
semantic_findings.description: add-component.sh and validate-module.sh interpolate MODULE_NAME into MODULE_PATH without applying the module-name validation present in create-module.sh. A caller can use ../ segments to write or scan outside frontend/src/modules.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow from MODULE_NAME to filesystem reads and writes is clear, and create-module.sh shows the intended validation pattern. Shell quoting reduces command injection risk but does not prevent path traversal.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time recreating module folders, starter files, and import patterns by hand. This skill creates consistent DevPrep AI modules and checks key TypeScript quality rules.
actual_capabilities: Creates feature module folders under the DevPrep AI frontend module path.
Generates starter TypeScript types, a component file, and barrel exports from templates.
Adds PascalCase component files to existing modules and updates component exports.
Validates module structure, file length, interface prefixes, any usage, and import patterns.
Provides references for architecture, naming conventions, path aliases, and quality checks.
limitations: Designed for the DevPrep AI frontend layout and repository depth.
Does not scaffold API endpoints, database models, or server modules.
Requires a Bash-compatible shell and the expected local project structure.
Generated files are starter templates and still need feature-specific logic.

use_cases.title: Create a New Feature Area
use_cases.description: Generate a clean module structure before implementing a new frontend domain such as analytics or notifications.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Additions
use_cases.description: Add new module components with consistent naming, TypeScript props, and barrel exports.

use_cases.title: Review Module Conventions
use_cases.description: Check a module against file size, naming, typing, and import rules before a code review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the module-scaffolder skill to create a notifications module. Show the generated structure and the next validation step.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a component to an existing module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a NotificationCard component to the notifications module. Keep the component name PascalCase and update exports.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Module Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Check an existing module before review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the analytics module with this skill. Summarize structure, typing, file size, and import issues found.

prompt_templates.title: Plan and Scaffold a Complex Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a larger feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a user-profile module, scaffold it, add ProfileCard and ProfileSettings components, then validate the result against the references.

output_examples.output: A new analytics module is created with components, hooks, utils, module types, and initial barrel exports.

output_examples.input: Add AnalyticsSummary to the analytics module.
output_examples.output: The component is added to the module components folder, and the component export list is updated.
The skill reports whether required folders, barrel exports, naming rules, type usage, and import patterns pass.

best_practices: Run scaffolding from the repository root so generated paths resolve correctly.
Use lowercase module names and PascalCase component names before running scripts.
Run validation after changing generated files and before requesting code review.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for repositories that do not match the DevPrep AI layout.
Do not treat generated templates as complete feature logic.
Do not bypass validation when adding cross-module imports or shared utilities.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it change existing files?
faq.answer: It can create new module files and append component exports in an existing module.

faq.question: Can it scaffold backend APIs?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on DevPrep AI frontend module folders and TypeScript starter files.

faq.question: Why does it emphasize path aliases?
faq.answer: The references guide users toward project aliases for cross-folder imports and relative imports inside a module.

faq.question: Is it useful outside DevPrep AI?
faq.answer: Only after adapting paths, templates, and quality rules to the target repository.

faq.question: What should users check after scaffolding?
faq.answer: Users should review generated names, add feature logic, run validation, and run the project test suite.
